chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Every comer has to return, and after returning it is as though he never existed.

key_terms.إِدْبَارٌ: Departure, leaving, or turning away (from the world)
key_terms.كَأَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ: As though he did not exist
key_terms.مُقْبِلٍ: One who enters or comes (towards the world/life)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'every comer has to return' mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this profound aphorism from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates the inevitability of death and the subsequent erasure of worldly memory, a concept deeply resonant with the Shia contemplation of *fana* (annihilation) and the transient nature of *dunya*. This saying serves as a spiritual reminder to prioritize eternal deeds over temporary status, reflecting the broader Islamic theme that true permanence lies in the Hereafter rather than earthly legacy. The emphasis on the 'negligibility' of the departed underscores the urgency of seizing the present moment for spiritual accumulation before one's time of departure arrives.
